first_impression.reaction: Googled 'getting married in hawaii' on the train. The intro gives me the whole process in one sentence: apply online, meet an agent together, marry with a licensed officiant within 30 days. No residency, no blood test. That's the answer, fast. It's written for Australians though, and I'm not one, so I had to work out which bits apply to me. Key Takeaways are short and clean. I jumped to the 'What to bring' list and then the FAQ. Bookmarked. The one thing I still don't know is how much the licence costs.

journey.quote: You apply online for a marriage licence, meet a licence agent together in person, and marry with a state-licensed officiant within the licence's 30 days.
journey.reaction: That's literally the answer I searched for, in the first paragraph. Good.

journey.quote: Getting married in Hawaii as an Australian couple is straightforward.
journey.reaction: Oh, it's for Australians. I'm in Singapore. Most of the Hawaii side probably applies to anyone, but now I'm second-guessing which bits are just for them.

journey.quote: You both meet a licence agent in person no sooner than 30 days before the ceremony, and the wedding must take place within 30 days of picking up the licence.
journey.reaction: Clear, and it's the bit that actually affects when we fly in. Useful.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Hawaii?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, to marry lawfully in Hawaii you need a marriage licence issued by an authorised agent of the Hawaii State Department of Health.
journey.reaction: Dated and linked to the actual Department page. That answers my 'is this still true' worry.

journey.quote: Complete the online marriage licence application at emrs.ehawaii.gov and pay the required fee.
journey.reaction: Just tell me how much it is. 'The required fee' on a how-to page feels like a dodge. Same with the certificate copies, 'a fee applies'.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Australians visiting the United States for less than 90 days may be eligible to apply for an Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) and enter under the Visa Waiver Program.
journey.reaction: ESTA and Smartraveller stuff before I even get to the licence. Not for me, and a lot of scrolling on a phone. Skipped.

journey.quote: A valid government-issued photo ID, such as a passport, for each applicant.
journey.reaction: Bold-led checklist, easy to screenshot. This is the section I'd actually come back to.

journey.section: Timing the appointment around your arrival
journey.quote: There is no waiting period once it is issued, so you can marry the next day if you choose.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. Nice, specific, useful.

journey.quote: On unencumbered State shoreline, yes: a right-of-entry permit through DLNR's Wiki Permits system, with a Certificate of Liability Insurance.
journey.reaction: Straight yes. The FAQ is short and answers the follow-ups I'd have Googled next.

journey.quote: Ask your officiant what the ceremony itself requires on the day, including witnesses, and how the marriage is registered afterwards.
journey.reaction: Asked a yes/no question about witnesses and got 'ask your officiant'. Bit of a letdown, though at least it's honest.

journey.section: Plan your Hawaii wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fine, clearly the sales bit at the end. 'Quotes in AUD' tells me again this is an Australian company. Doesn't say what anything costs.

turn_offs_found.quote: Complete the online marriage licence application at emrs.ehawaii.gov and pay the required fee.
turn_offs_found.why: The first thing I want from a how-to is the cost. 'The required fee' with no number sends me back to Google.

turn_offs_found.quote: Start with the travel side, because it has its own lead time.
turn_offs_found.why: The ESTA, e-Passport and Smartraveller section sits before the licence steps. It's long on a phone and off my question, so the main answer is pushed further down.

would_share_with: My partner, the Key Takeaways and the 'What to bring' list, as a screenshot

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-hawaii&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I came for the legal steps and got them. I don't know this brand, it seems aimed at Australians, and I'm nowhere near choosing a planner. Bookmark, not enquiry.

top_3_changes: State the licence and certified-copy fees as dollar figures with an 'as at' date, if the Department publishes them, or say plainly where to check. 'The required fee' reads like the page is hiding the number.
Move or shorten the ESTA and Smartraveller section so the licence steps come sooner on mobile, for example a short 'Before you go' box after the licence steps.
Add one line near the top saying the Hawaii steps apply to any overseas couple and only the 'back home' sections are Australia-specific, so non-Australian searchers don't bounce.
